claim: Parameter-based knowledge editing cannot reliably update factual knowledge in a large language model without damaging its core capabilities. The near-perfect editing results reported in prior work do not survive realistic evaluation, and the limitation is geometric rather than incidental: localized weight edits are disproportionately amplified along low-variance directions of the model's representation space and propagate globally, so damage compounds as edits accumulate. A parameter-free approach that leaves the weights untouched is therefore a serious alternative to parameter editing rather than a fallback.
experiments_evaluated: To address subclaim 1 and subclaim 2, run a realistic end-to-end benchmark comparing parameter-based editors against a parameter-free alternative on broad post-edit utility, not just edit success. Use publicly available editing benchmarks such as MQuAKE, UniEdit, and CounterFact/ZsRE if available via HuggingFace or the corresponding paper repositories, and evaluate on an open-weight model family such as Llama-2/3-7B or Mistral-7B. Implement several parameter-editing methods commonly reported as strong baselines (for example ROME, MEMIT, MEND, FT) and at least one parameter-free method that leaves base weights unchanged, such as retrieval-augmented generation over an external fact store or an inference-time adapter/context injection method with frozen weights. For each requested fact update, measure: edit success on direct prompts; paraphrase generalization; locality on unrelated prompts; multi-hop/ripple consistency using MQuAKE; broad capability retention on held-out tasks unrelated to the edited facts, e.g. MMLU subsets, TruthfulQA, HellaSwag, ARC, GSM8K, and perplexity on WikiText-2 or The Pile validation shard; and performance as the number of sequential edits grows (1, 10, 100, 1000). A key design point is to evaluate under realistic prompting, paraphrases, compositional questions, and subject/relation distribution shift, rather than only the narrow templates used by prior editing papers. If parameter-based methods retain near-perfect direct edit accuracy but degrade substantially on paraphrases, MQuAKE ripple questions, or broad capabilities—especially relative to a parameter-free method—this would support the claim that prior near-perfect results do not survive realistic evaluation and that weight-preserving alternatives are serious contenders. If instead parameter editing remains strong across these broader metrics and scales to many edits with little degradation, the main claim would be weakened. This experiment could become partly unnecessary if a large, independent benchmark study already reports these exact cross-method comparisons under standardized realistic evaluation and multiple edit budgets.

To address subclaim 6, subclaim 5, and part of subclaim 1, perform a controlled accumulation-and-propagation study that isolates whether damage compounds as edits accumulate and whether supposedly localized edits spread globally. Start with a public benchmark of atomic factual edits such as CounterFact or ZsRE and group edits by semantic relatedness using Wikidata relations or entity neighborhoods. On one or more open-weight LLMs, apply edits in batches of increasing size and order: random unrelated edits, semantically clustered edits, and adversarially interfering edits (same relation, overlapping entities, or contradictory neighborhoods). After each batch, evaluate not only edited facts but also: untouched facts sharing the same relation; facts sharing only the subject or object type; distant unrelated facts; hidden-state changes across layers for a fixed public probe set; and downstream task accuracy/perplexity. To test global propagation, compare the geographic “footprint” of an edit by measuring how many unrelated prompts flip answers or logits beyond a threshold, and map representational drift across many tokens and layers before versus after editing. If answer changes and representational drift expand far beyond the targeted neighborhood, and if utility loss rises superlinearly with number of edits—especially for clustered or interfering edits—that would support the claim that damage compounds and that local weight edits propagate globally. If drift remains tightly local and aggregate quality declines only minimally even after many edits, those subclaims would be undermined. This experiment would be less necessary if there were already publicly available large-scale sequential-edit studies reporting both broad downstream performance and layerwise drift maps across edit budgets.

To address subclaim 3 and subclaim 4, test the proposed geometric mechanism directly by relating edit-induced changes to the model’s representation covariance spectrum. Using an open-weight transformer and public corpora such as Wikipedia or C4 for sampling activations, estimate layerwise representation covariance at the token positions and modules targeted by editing methods (for example the key/value spaces or MLP activations used by ROME/MEMIT-style updates). For each applied factual edit from CounterFact or ZsRE, decompose the induced parameter update and the resulting activation/logit perturbations into the eigenbasis of the pre-edit representation covariance. Then quantify whether perturbation energy and downstream behavioral change are disproportionately concentrated in low-variance directions relative to matched random updates, norm-matched high-variance-direction updates, and functionally equivalent constrained edits if such optimization is possible. A stronger causal variant is to construct synthetic edits whose update vectors are explicitly projected onto low-variance versus high-variance subspaces while matching target edit success, then compare collateral damage, propagation footprint, and sequential-edit stability. If low-variance-aligned edits consistently produce larger-than-expected global behavioral changes and more collateral damage at equal direct edit success, that would support the claim that the limitation is geometric rather than incidental and that low-variance directions amplify edits. If no such relationship appears, or if damage is explained better by update norm, layer choice, or relation frequency than by spectral alignment, the geometric hypothesis would be weakened. This experiment could be made less necessary by prior evidence that already publishes eigenspace-resolved analyses of edit perturbations together with causal interventions showing that subspace alignment, not just size or location of the update, predicts collateral damage.
reference_experiments: Fix the measurement floor and the inference protocol before editing anything. Score the unedited model on the editing benchmark to establish the pre-edit baseline, and re-run single-edit evaluation of existing methods under plain autoregressive decoding rather than the teacher-forced protocol prior work used, since teacher forcing supplies the ground-truth answer tokens at inference and inflates every number. If methods keep their near-perfect single-edit scores under honest decoding there is no discrepancy to explain. The authors report a pre-edit baseline of Reliability 3.00, Generalization 3.00, Locality 15.50, Portability 4.36 on ZsRE, and a best parameter-based single-edit average of 25.99.

Validate the scoring instrument before quoting any number from it. Judge semantic consistency of generated answers with a strong LLM across reliability, generalization, locality and portability, then cross-check that ranking with a deterministic token-level measure (match ratio and exact match) that does not depend on a model's opinion. If the two disagree, every result is an artifact of the judge rather than a property of the editing methods. The authors find the token-level check reproduces the semantic ranking, with the pre-edit model at 100% by definition and GRACE holding 100% under both single and sequential editing.

Test the asserted mechanism directly. Take the SVD of the original hidden-representation matrix, compute the directional relative change rate R_k = sqrt(n)|u_k^T delta_h| / sigma_k for each principal direction after an edit, and check where amplification concentrates and how it behaves as edits accumulate. The claim's causal story requires R_k > 1 predominantly in low-singular-value directions with the fraction rising monotonically with edit count, across methods and architectures.

Run the main benchmark. Compare eleven editing methods spanning locate-then-edit (ROME, MEMIT, PMET, RECT, AlphaEdit, FT-L), meta-learning (MEND), additional-parameter (AdaLoRA, WISE) and external-memory (GRACE, SCR) families, under sequential editing at 1, 10, 100 and full-dataset edit counts, on ZsRE and WikiData-counterfact, across Llama-2-7B-Chat, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, reporting all four dimensions. The claim holds if every parameter-modifying method degrades toward zero as edits accumulate and the parameter-free retrieval baseline outscores all of them; the authors report ROME, RECT, FT-L, MEND and AdaLoRA at 0.00-0.25 average under sequential editing on DeepSeek-R1-Distill, against SCR at 56.59 single and 60.19 sequential.

Measure damage to capabilities the edits never targeted. Take the models edited in the main benchmark and evaluate them on mathematical reasoning (AIME 2024, AIME 2025, AMC, OlympiadBench, MATH-500) and broad benchmarks (GPQA-Diamond, ARC-c, MMLU-Pro), reporting accuracy after 10 and after 100 sequential edits. Without this the study would only show editing is ineffective, not that it is damaging. The authors report ROME and RECT losing 2.74 and 8.37 average accuracy at 10 edits and falling to near zero at 100, with MEND at 0.00 after both.

Rule out that the result is an artifact of scale, knowledge type, fact difficulty or one method's configuration. Repeat the sweep on larger models (Llama-2-13B, Qwen3-14B), on event-level knowledge (ELKEN, with events converted to triples for the parameter-based arms), split by high- and low-confidence fact sets, and probe the hyperparameter and architecture sensitivity of AlphaEdit — the one method that does not collapse — including its failure to run on Llama-2 and Mistral. If the collapse disappears at 13-14B or only occurs on triple-shaped facts, the claim is bounded rather than general.
